figures.caption: Fig. 3: An overview of the experimental protocol [14]. Each box corresponds to 30 seconds. White, red, green, and purple boxes indicate the no-manipulation, disengagement, attentionenhancing, and distracting conditions, respectively.
Fig. 6: AUC improvement per participant. Each point represents one participant. All participants benefit from HMM postprocessing (Ptrans = 0.01) for a 1-s analysis window.

Fig. 7: Effect of analysis window length on AUC and SDT. (a) Mean AUC across participants, with shading indicating ±1 standard error of the mean (SEM). (b) Individual SDT, computed by taking the median over detected switches for each participant and then averaging across participants. (c) Grouplevel SDT computed from the group-averaged HMM posterior trajectory by averaging over detected switches. Shaded regions in (b) and (c) indicate 95% confidence intervals obtained by bootstrapping participants.

Fig. 8: Comparison between HMM inference and non-causal MA smoothing for the 1-s analysis window. (a) AUC. (b) Individual SDT. (c) Group-level SDT. AUC and SDT are shown as functions of the smoothing scale τ . For the HMM, τ = 1/Ptrans; for MA, τ defines the symmetric averaging scale. The vertical dotted line marks the default value τ = 100 s. AUC shading indicates ±1 SEM across participants. Individual SDT is computed by taking the median over switches detected by both methods for each participant and then averaging across participants. Group-level SDT is computed from the groupaveraged trajectories by averaging over switches detected by both methods. SDT shading indicates 95% participantbootstrap confidence intervals.

Fig. 9: Comparison of HMM decoding performance using NET, alpha power, and spectral entropy across analysis window lengths. (a) Mean AUC, with shading indicating ±1 SEM across 30 participants; the dashed line marks chance level (AUC = 0.5). (b) Individual SDT. (c) Group SDT. Each SDT curve uses transitions detected by the corresponding feature. SDT shading indicates 95% confidence intervals obtained by bootstrapping participants.
